The situation is dramatic. I'm not speaking specifically about Cannes, because Cannes has shown resilience by refusing to fully embrace films from streaming platforms. But many other festivals are becoming simply the final stage of the promotional campaign for films that receive a brief theatrical release before moving almost immediately onto streaming services. Festivals were originally meant to reveal the market value of films beyond their immediate artistic qualities. When I was running Locarno, for instance, the purpose of the Piazza Grande wasn't to show films already acquired by Swiss distributors. We wanted to present films that distributors from Switzerland, Italy, France, Germany and elsewhere in Europe could still discover and acquire. And it worked. [...] Festivals should reveal the future of cinema, not become the last stop before streaming. Today, I feel many are betraying what their original mission should have been.

I wanted these famous music trivia questions and answers to feel like listening to a very unpredictable playlist. The trivia section already moves across decades, countries, landmarks, history, geography, and general knowledge, while this collection stays firmly focused on music. One question may bring up Louis Armstrong, another Eminem, another ABBA, another Dolly Parton, another the Spice Girls. The song changes before the quiz has time to become repetitive.

The songs aren’t repeated later simply so the same artist-song connection can be asked in reverse. Artists can appear more than once when they have several genuinely famous songs, but each of the 300 questions is built around a different track. [...] That period is one reason the 2000s are especially fun for me, but this round goes much further than one decade, even if that decade is the 2010s. These music trivia questions for adults move between old standards, Motown, rock, pop, musicals, dance music, movie soundtracks, and global hits. The songs are still recognizable; now knowing the artist isn’t always enough.

Question 101: Whitney Houston made this ballad a global phenomenon in The Bodyguard. Which country star wrote and first released it?  
 Answer: Dolly Parton.

Question 102: Which artist made “Purple Rain” both a signature song and the title of his 1984 film and album?  
 Answer: Prince. [...] ID 137182227 ©Arne9001 | Dreamstime.com

Cable television changed music for me again. Suddenly there were entire channels devoted to music videos, and I was fascinated. I still remember going from a black-and-white television to a color one and finally seeing what all those videos actually looked like. It made the songs feel bigger somehow.

Many of those unforgettable videos came from British artists, which is one reason UK trivia overlaps so naturally with music history. The final round uses hard music trivia questions and answers about songs that stayed famous: writers, samples, unexpected collaborators, music videos, soundtracks, recording stories, and other connections that can give you a very satisfying “I knew that!” moment.

# Ultra rare Nintendo Mario game cartridges discovered in Wisconsin

A set of unique, extremely rare Super Mario cartridges was found in a gaming store in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and will be auctioned off starting Friday

AUSTIN, Texas -- A few years ago, a pop culture store owner in Wisconsin mentioned to Jason Ganos, a well-known Nintendo game collector, that he had a box of Super Mario cartridges that had been sitting in storage for years. It stopped Ganos in his tracks.

It would turn out to be an ultra rare collection, Ganos said. The cartridges will go up for sale Friday in an online auction that will run until Sept. 9. [...] “I still don’t quite believe that any of this is happening,” Ganos said. “I just think it’s kind of serendipitous that this happened. It’s just still very bizarre to me.”

Ganos, a hard-core fan covered in Nintendo tattoos and who has operated Nintendo Wire, a news service for Nintendo announcements and nostalgia for over 10 years, said he would not venture to guess how much the games are worth.

But when he saw the box, he immediately knew it was special.

“It’s like pulling out like a Holy Grail,” Ganos said, later adding “they're gorgeous.”

The discovery came after the owner, Kevin Braun, of One Stop Wonders in Waukesha, outside Milwaukee, asked Ganos to help him sell some stuff, including common Nintendo games and Pokémon cards.

## Next steps and industry questions

The deal remains subject to remaining regulatory approvals and ongoing litigation.

In July 2026, attorneys general from 12 states sued to block the acquisition, arguing that the merger would reduce competition in film distribution, cable television, and streaming.A federal judge subsequently issued a temporary restraining order preventing the transaction from closing for 14 days. Paramount disputed the allegations and said it would vigorously defend the merger.

Regulatory reviews also remained underway in the European Union and the United Kingdom. [...] Paramount then launched a hostile bid for the entire company, offering $30 a share and appealing directly to shareholders. Warner’s board rejected the bid and reaffirmed its support for the Netflix agreement. In February, Paramount raised its offer to $31 a share. Warner’s board determined that the revised proposal constituted a “superior proposal” under its merger agreement with Netflix.

On February 26, 2026, Netflix said it wouldn’t match the revised bid, effectively ending its pursuit of Warner.

In April 2026, Warner shareholders approved Paramount’s $31-a-share acquisition of the company, valuing the deal at about $81 billion, or roughly $111 billion including debt. The U.S. Department of Justice approved the deal a month later.

## Next steps and industry questions [...] Should the deal close, Paramount faces the task of integrating Warner’s studios, streaming services, and cable networks while maintaining ongoing film and television production. The combination would reshape the competitive landscape, creating a larger rival to Walt Disney (DIS), Netflix, and Amazon.com (AMZN) at a time when the industry is still adjusting to streaming-driven shifts in viewing habits.

The outcome also raises broader questions:

The answers will shape not only the future of the two companies but also the direction of the entertainment business.

## COVID couldn’t stop it, and neither can screens

Goodtimes said the COVID-19 pandemic did not slow the game’s momentum. Leagues moved to Zoom and drew large audiences.

> “We actually had these leagues running, and we were playing on Zoom, and it was huge.”

Now that bars are fully open again, Quizzo has returned in force. Goodtimes, reflecting on more than 20 years of hosting, said the game fills a need that screens cannot.

> “I think there’s something kind of magic in a society where people are kind of perpetually online, that it’s an excuse to get together in person and enjoy your friends in person.” [...] Some nights carry specific themes. Bourbon & Branch runs a music-themed Quizzo on Tuesdays with a $50 cash prize. The Pub on Passyunk East hosts a monthly ’80s-to-2000s pop culture edition. At New Wave Cafe in Bella Vista, one round follows a “connections” format where players earn bonus points for finding links between their answers.

Team sizes generally cap at six to eight players, and most events are free to enter. Many bars run food and drink specials during the game to draw crowds on slower weeknights.

The guide notes it will be updated as new Quizzo nights are added. Players looking for the latest schedule can also check individual venues’ social media pages or consult The Quizzo List spreadsheet.

If you have spent any time in a Philadelphia bar on a weeknight, you have probably heard the word “Quizzo.” The team trivia game is a fixture at hundreds of restaurants and bars across the city, running every night of the week. But the name itself is a Philly original, with roots that stretch back to a Jersey Shore bar in the early 1990s.

A comprehensive guide published by Billy Penn traces the game’s history and maps out dozens of active Quizzo nights across the city, including at least one spot in Northeast Philadelphia.
